title: Encapsulation path flap causing tenant egress misrouting and intermittent DNS blackholes
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent 5xxs and DNS failures for tenant egress traffic after recent overlay kernel updates. Traffic for affected tenants was misrouted through an outdated encapsulation path, causing asymmetric return paths and, in some cases, DNS responses to be dropped by downstream NAT/edge devices. This ticket tracks the investigation, hotfix rollout, and preventive changes to eliminate recurrence.
reproduction_steps: 1) Provision a dedicated tenant in staging with VPC peering to vpc-staging-eu
2) Apply overlay kernel vX.Y.Z with the new path selection heuristic enabled
3) Generate sustained outbound UDP DNS queries from tenant hosts (udp port 53) to an external resolver
4) Observe intermittent DNS timeouts and packet captures showing return packets with old encapsulation headers not recognized by current SNAT table
impact_summary: Impact observed across 3 paying Dedicated customers (two in EU region, one in us-west). Symptoms: elevated DNS query latency, transient DNS resolution failures leading to API 5xxs for LLM-serving endpoints. Estimated affected TPS at peak: ~150 requests/sec across tenants. Customer reports include degraded SLA and one support escalation to SOC.
triage_notes: On-call network lead reproduced DNS blackholes in staging. Initial scope bound to overlay path selection after last kernel bump (2026-02-20). Not a control-plane config change. High likelihood of race between encap cache invalidation and BGP/route convergence when peering flaps occur.
root_cause: A regression in the overlay path selection heuristic allowed stale encap nexthop entries to persist when an L2/L3 peering transient occurred. Requests were forwarded with legacy encapsulation indices; edge SNAT devices only accept current encap profiles, causing asymmetric droppage for UDP responses. Additionally, our resolver redispatch logic retried via the same stale path rather than falling back to an alternative route.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Reverted kernel heuristics on affected nodes (hotfix kernel-rollback vX.Y.Z->vX.Y.Z-1) — deployed to 60% of impacted fleet
2) Temporarily disabled aggressive encap cache retention (ttl override to 30s) via runtime flag
3) Applied a dynamic SNAT acceptance rule patch on edge boxes to accept legacy encap markers for a 24 hour migration window
deployment_plan: Phased rollout: 1) complete hotfix kernel rollback across remaining 40% of affected nodes (3 hours), 2) verify DNS resolution and egress paths for test tenants, 3) flip encap-cache-ttl back to low once stable, 4) schedule permanent heuristic fix in next minor release.
testing_plan: Automated testcases added to e2e-network-suite: (a) simulate peering flap and assert encapsulation indices are recomputed, (b) UDP DNS request/response validation across SNAT edge, (c) resilience test with rapid peering churn. Manual smoke test with customer-representative traffic profiles planned in staging and canary before full prod rollout.
rollback_plan: If DNS errors do not fall within 30 minutes post-rollback on a canary cohort, revert kernel to pre-bump image and re-enable prior SNAT policy; notify customers and open incident call.
long_term_actions: 1) Implement stronger encap cache invalidation tied to peering state changes (watch peering BGP session state) — engineering follow-up
2) Add telemetry: encap index age, peering-state-change events, and DNS-response asymmetry metrics in Console
3) Harden resolver redispatch to consider alternative egress paths on repeated UDP failures
4) Postmortem and runbook update for peering flaps affecting dedicated tenants
notes: Security reviewed the temporary SNAT acceptance rule and approved for 24h as mitigation. We coordinated with affected customers; one requested extended rollover window which has been granted until 2026-03-07. On-call remains on 24/7 watch until full remediation.
